title: Canadian novelist removed from Prix Goncourt longlist after AI allegations

reading.body:
This is a case of contested attribution rather than a confirmed deployment failure. The public claim rests on a detector score circulated in a social media post, and the reporting that followed examined the author's earlier writing for plagiarism. No system output is described as having been used in the writing itself, and no technical evaluation of the novel is reported.

The removal happened at the level of a prize longlist, not at a publisher, a platform, or a production pipeline. The Académie Goncourt acted on its own review of the allegations and cited both the prize's integrity and the apparent plagiarism in earlier work. The author's publishers denied the AI claims, and his Quebec publisher stopped promoting the book while stating it could not confirm AI use. That is the shape of the problem: a decision was taken on allegations that the parties closest to the work say they cannot verify.

Catching this kind of dispute would require evidence of how the text was produced, which the reporting does not provide. A detector score alone is not that evidence, and the outlets do not report any examination of drafts, process, or provenance. It is not established that AI was used, that the detector was accurate, or that the plagiarism finding in the earlier work has been adjudicated by anyone.

reports.title: Canadian novelist removed from Prix Goncourt longlist after AI allegations

summary:
The Prix Goncourt, France's top literary prize, removed Canadian author Thélyson Orélien's novel from its longlist after reviewing AI allegations. The Académie Goncourt said the decision protects the prize's integrity and that Orélien's earlier work appeared to contain plagiarism. His novel, C'était ça ou mourir, was his first and had been sold to 23 countries, with an English edition planned for 2028.

Orélien and his French publisher denied the AI claims, and his Quebec publisher halted promotion while saying it could not confirm AI use. The allegations followed a social media post citing a detector score and a La Presse investigation into his past writing. The prize will be awarded in early November.
